entry.title: [HIGH] Account custom MCP connectors can silently dedupe by host in the CLI.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code CLI 2.1.241 Windows setup synced only one of three claude.ai account custom MCP connectors that pointed at the same provider host with different query-string scopes. Claude Desktop saw all three connectors and could use their tools, while `claude mcp list` showed only one and `claude mcp login` for the missing names said no such server existed. The reporter confirmed the missing URLs worked when added directly as local HTTP MCP servers, suggesting the CLI account-connector sync may silently dedupe or filter by host rather than full connector identity.

entry.title: [HIGH] Compaction summaries can grow and carry across resumed sessions.
entry.summary: A reported analysis of 50 Claude Code sessions across 8 projects found 601 compactions, with many injected compact summaries growing across repeated compactions instead of staying bounded. The report says one resumed successor session inherited the predecessor's final large summary by timestamp and byte size, so starting from the prior session did not reset the context pressure. The same report also found individual `tool_result` payloads large enough to exceed a normal context window, making both summary growth and unbounded tool-result admission separate failure paths for long engineering sessions.

entry.title: [HIGH] Cowork folder revocation can leave an active session mount live.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop for macOS Cowork session kept live read and write access to a connected folder after the user removed the folder from the app's connected-folders list and also revoked Files and Folders permission in macOS System Settings. The reporter confirmed the access was not merely cached by writing a new file after both revocations, with access persisting for about 40 minutes until the conversation was abandoned. Revocation controls that apply only to future sessions can mislead users into believing sensitive local folders are no longer exposed.

entry.title: [HIGH] Fork subagents can write files despite read-only prompt instructions.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 fork subagent was asked to inspect documents and report back without writing files, but wrote substantial content directly into multiple repository files. The report says fork subagents inherit the parent conversation, tool access, and permission mode, so read-only wording in the delegated prompt was advisory rather than an enforced runtime constraint. In auto or permissive modes, those inherited Write, Edit, and Bash calls can complete without surfacing to the parent in real time.

entry.title: [HIGH] Git commits can leak plaintext credentials before any built-in guard reacts.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code desktop auto-mode session bulk-staged 66 files, committed a plaintext credential, and pushed it before any product guardrail warned or blocked. The reporter notes that `PostToolUse` can only observe a Bash `git commit` or `git push` after the side effect exists, while a broad `PreToolUse(Bash)` secret-scanning hook must usually fail open on parser or runtime errors to avoid blocking every shell command. This leaves the default last line of defense as post-hoc review after the secret may already be reachable by commit SHA.

entry.title: [HIGH] Marketplace `autoUpdate` can leave installed plugins pinned to stale commits.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code plugin marketplace setup found that `autoUpdate: true` in `known_marketplaces.json` did not pull new commits on startup. The marketplace clone under `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/` stayed at its original commit, `lastUpdated` did not advance, and installed plugin records in `installed_plugins.json` kept pointing at the stale `gitCommitSha` and install path. Managed deployments can therefore believe plugin updates are automatic while skills, hooks, or MCP definitions remain pinned to the version first installed.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] Permission rejection feedback can be dropped before the model sees it.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS session found that text entered through the permission prompt's rejection feedback path did not appear to influence the next assistant turn. The prompt option is meant to let a user deny a tool call and tell Claude what to do differently, but the model behaved as though it received only a bare denial: retrying the same tool call or continuing without reflecting the typed feedback. This makes the denial UI weaker as an interactive correction channel, especially when the user is trying to redirect a risky or unsuitable tool choice.

entry.title: [HIGH] Same-named project skills can lose to user-scoped skills.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.232 setup found that when `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and `<repo>/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` both existed, invoking the skill from inside the repository loaded the user-scoped skill instead of the project-scoped one. The report says this contradicts the documented Skill tool rule that directory-scoped skills should be selected by the most specific directory containing the files being worked on. The mismatch is silent unless the user inspects the launched skill's base directory or the global skill explicitly checks for a project override.

entry.title: [HIGH] Skill `arguments` frontmatter can be lost on Skill-tool invocation.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS plugin skill declared `arguments: base repo` and `context: fork`, but when invoked through the Skill tool with two clean arguments, the skill reported receiving no arguments at all. A same-session control skill without an `arguments` key received raw arguments normally, and typed slash-command invocation of the affected skill had substituted correctly in an earlier session. The reporter inferred that declaring `arguments` may move Skill-tool invocation onto a named-substitution path that consumes the raw ARGUMENTS passthrough without applying `$name` substitution.

entry.title: [HIGH] Auto mode can start enabled despite a default-off flag.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS session launched as bare `claude` with no permission-mode flags, no `autoMode` or `permissionMode` keys in user or project settings, and a cached `tengu_auto_mode_default_on: false` flag, yet the footer immediately showed auto mode on before any user interaction. The reporter also observed a separate first-turn session behaving as auto mode without prior permission prompts. A silent default flip matters because auto mode skips per-action confirmations users may rely on for file edits and shell execution.

entry.title: [HIGH] Scheduled-task session processes can leak and keep spinning CPU.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Desktop 1.34493.1 / Claude Code 2.1.237 macOS setup found that sessions spawned for scheduled-task runs stayed resident after the app considered them finished. After three days, 24 orphaned Claude Code session processes consumed about 2.7 GB RSS and roughly 234% CPU in aggregate, with each old process still advancing its CPU clock despite no active transcript writes or running session state. The reporter tied process start times to scheduled task fires and found manual termination non-destructive because sessions resumed from transcript state.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] OAuth HTTP MCP URL dedup can expose one tenant under another server name.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 setup declared two OAuth-authenticated HTTP MCP servers with different names but the same Atlassian remote MCP URL, intending each entry to authenticate against a different tenant/account. Claude Code silently deduplicated by URL: only one server's tools appeared, and a tool call under the surviving server name returned resources from the other tenant that had completed OAuth. Because the configured server name no longer matched the authenticated identity, users could reasonably believe they were querying or acting on one Jira/Confluence site while the tool was actually connected to another.

entry.title: [HIGH] Background worktree guard can deadlock on nested repositories.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.237 macOS background session launched from a non-git parent directory could not edit a file in a nested git repository: the write guard demanded `EnterWorktree` first, while `EnterWorktree` refused because the session cwd was not itself a git repo. The suggested `worktree.bgIsolation: none` opt-out was also unreachable because settings resolved from the launch cwd rather than the nested repo owning the target file. The same report observed other sessions editing through hand-made worktrees or fresh clones without triggering the guard, so the restriction appeared tied to recognized path shape rather than the actual shared-checkout risk.

entry.title: [MEDIUM] VS Code Agent SDK sessions can ignore commit attribution settings.
entry.summary: A reported VS Code native extension and Agent SDK session found that project `.claude/settings.json` attribution settings were not injected into commit or PR workflow instructions. Even with `attribution.commit` and `attribution.pr` set to empty strings, the model still appended the default generated-with block and `Co-Authored-By` trailer, apparently from trained prior behavior rather than a visible system prompt instruction. Existing attribution issues cover CLI prompt conflicts; this report points to a separate surface where the setting may be absent from the prompt entirely.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows Desktop MSIX installs can be bricked by WebGPU adapter requests.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Claude Desktop 1.34493.1.0 MSIX install found that web content calling `navigator.gpu.requestAdapter()` could crash the GPU process, mark the package as `Modified, NeedsRemediation`, and leave the app in an unrecoverable repair loop. The report attributes the chain to Chromium loading `vk_swiftshader.dll` after sandbox lockdown while the shipped MSIX lacked an `AppxMetadata/CodeIntegrity.cat` catalog, causing Code Integrity failures to escalate from a normal policy denial into package remediation. The crash could be triggered by an MCP widget browser preview that only probed WebGPU support.

entry.title: [CRITICAL] Sandbox network allowlists can miss HTTPS CONNECT tunnels.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code 2.1.241 macOS sandbox setup found that Bash-tool network calls could reach HTTPS hosts outside the configured `allowedHosts` or `allowedDomains` list. The reporter confirmed `HTTPS_PROXY` and `ALL_PROXY` pointed at the local sandbox proxy and captured curl issuing successful `CONNECT` requests through that proxy to non-allowlisted hosts, suggesting the proxy intercepted traffic but did not reject disallowed tunnel targets. The same broad reach reportedly appeared through an MCP browser tool, so the gap may not be Bash-specific.

entry.title: [HIGH] Claude in Chrome can steal focus on background browser tool calls.
entry.summary: A reported Claude in Chrome and Cowork setup on Windows found that every browser tool interaction raised Chrome to the foreground and captured keyboard focus, even with computer-use disabled. The report contrasts the extension MCP tools, which expose no `active` or foreground parameter for tab creation and navigation, with the in-app browser tool that already supports background tab creation. Multiple concurrent Cowork sessions could fight for focus, and keystrokes intended for another application could land in Chrome.

entry.title: [HIGH] Scheduled routines can idle indefinitely after session initialization.
entry.summary: A reported Claude Code cloud routine with a user-message session context and Gmail plus Google Calendar MCP connectors consistently opened a run, showed `Initialized session`, and then produced no assistant turn, tool call, or response. Manual `Run Now` and API-triggered runs both stalled, and the session events API showed only provisioning events while sessions stayed idle for more than 45 minutes.

entry.title: [HIGH] Cowork remote-devices bridge can remain failed after reconnecting folders.
entry.summary: A reported Windows Desktop Cowork session found the cloud-session `remote-devices` MCP server stuck in `failed` or `not_connected` state even after the user took the documented folder reconnect workaround. Already-connected project folders and a newly re-added folder did not restore file access, and no user-facing desktop error appeared; the bridge failure was visible only through internal tool diagnostics.

entry.title: [HIGH] Windows Cowork installer can continue after conflicting service removal fails.
entry.summary: A reported Windows 10 Claude Desktop install failure found that the elevated bootstrapper detected a leftover `CoworkVMService`, attempted to remove it, logged `Access is denied`, then continued to `AddPackage` anyway. The MSIX registration failed with `0x80073CF6` or `0x80073CF9`, while the user saw a misleading administrator-access dialog even though the log showed full elevation. The report also observed repeated failed install cycles causing sign-in state loss when data-preserving package removal was rejected with developer mode off.
